title: Efficacy and Safety of Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir Alafenamide (B/F/TAF) in People with HIV-1 After Bariatric Surgery – A Multicenter Retrospective German Cohort Study
summary:
Research Question:
Can sustained viral suppression be achieved in people with HIV who have undergone weight-loss surgery, such as gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy, and are being treated with Biktarvy, despite potentially reduced absorption and metabolism of the active ingredients?

Background:
As life expectancy increases, so does the prevalence of overweight and obesity among people with HIV. Obesity not only poses a high risk for cardiovascular and metabolic diseases but also increasingly influences therapeutic decisions in long-term HIV treatment.
The treatment of obesity through surgery, such as sleeve gastrectomy or gastric bypass (so-called bariatric surgeries), alters the structure and function of the digestive tract. This can significantly affect the absorption of medications. This is particularly important in HIV therapy, as reduced absorption of the active ingredients may lead to insufficient suppression of the virus and to resistance to the active ingredients.
Bictegravir, a component of the Biktarvy tablet, is highly effective. Resistance also does not develop as quickly.
However, studies show that the effectiveness of bictegravir may be reduced under certain conditions, particularly when taken concurrently with dietary supplements such as calcium and magnesium.
Following bariatric surgery, these dietary supplements are used on a long-term basis.
In addition, a slight reduction in the effectiveness of bictegravir has been reported in patients with higher body weight.
Evidence of Biktarvy’s efficacy and safety following bariatric surgery is currently limited. Therefore, there is a need to collect and analyze data from a larger patient cohort.

Method:
The study aims to collect and analyze data from the past five years—already gathered in routine clinical practice at several German centers—on HIV patients who underwent bariatric surgery and were treated with Biktarvy. Treatment may have been initiated either before bariatric surgery and continued afterward, or it may have been initiated only after the procedure. The data will be collected at specified time points following the bariatric surgery. Data collection is anonymous; therefore, it is not possible to identify individual patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Included are persons of legal age with a confirmed HIV-1 infection and a history of bariatric surgery, such as sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, who treated with B/F/TAF. Treatment may have started before bariatric surgery and continued afterward, or it may have been started after the procedure. At least one documented HIV-1 RNA < 200 copies/ml within six months before surgery or before the start of B/F/TAF and at least one documented HIV-1 RNA measurement after surgery or after treatment start are required.
Exclusion criteria:
Excluded are persons under 18 years of age, persons who were not treated with B/F/TAF during the relevant observation period, and cases with a follow-up of less than six months that is insufficient for the endpoint assessment.
